title: The Final Vector
premise: Freya Quintana navigates the Meridian, a freighter whose hold holds illegal memory-backups of the crew of a ship that was supposedly never lost. When gravity stutters across the Halcyon system for nine seconds, her vessel is dragged into a quarantine zone where an entire colony's massacre has been erased from every archive. Pursued by the Bureau of Continuity and betrayed by a captain who sold them out to protect his own backups, Freya must recover the erased records hidden inside one of the sleeping copies — her own. In the end she broadcasts the truth at the cost of her memories of everyone she loves, choosing that others remember even if she cannot.
about_author: Sebastian Reyes is a former maritime cartographer who turned to science fiction after mapping shipping lanes through disputed waters for a decade. He writes about people who keep systems running in places where the truth has been rerouted.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Silence
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Running the dead route between non-communicating worlds, Freya feels gravity flicker for exactly nine seconds and fights to keep the Meridian from tearing apart. The beat is dread: something impossible just happened, and every instrument insists nothing did.

chapters.title: The Hold We Don't Open
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, with flashbacks. She checks on the illegal memory-backups sleeping in the hold — including one labeled with her own name — while Captain Osei orders silence about the anomaly. The emotional beat is guilt: she knows what they're carrying and why it damns them all.

chapters.title: Quarantine Line
chapters.summary: Engineer Sefa's POV. The Meridian is intercepted at the edge of the Vesper colony system, officially uninhabited for sixty years, by Bureau ships demanding they turn back. Sefa notices the colony's orbital debris is far too fresh. The beat is suspicion hardening into certainty.

chapters.title: What the Records Say
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Docking under false pretenses at a relay station, Freya finds archives describing Vesper as a thriving world until a clean, documented evacuation. But the timestamps are impossible — files dated after the station itself went dark. The beat is vertigo: reality's paperwork doesn't match reality.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold the Sky
chapters.summary: Captain Osei's POV. Revealed: Osei has been feeding their route data to the Bureau in exchange for keeping his own backup out of the incinerator. He believes he's protecting the crew. The beat is tragic compromise — power corrupting a decent man one small permission at a time.

chapters.title: Ghosts in the Lattice
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Hiding in the debris field, Freya interfaces with the backups and wakes a fragment of the Vesper massacre recorded inside one of them — her own past self witnessed it. The beat is horror and recognition: she is evidence, and the Bureau knows it.

chapters.title: Bureau of Continuity
chapters.summary: Inspector Vale's POV. The antagonist hunts the Meridian, believing erasure is mercy — that a species that remembers its massacres tears itself apart. Vale's chapters make the enemy sympathetic and wrong. The beat is chilling conviction.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. A desperate descent through Vesper's atmosphere to find physical records the digital purge missed, pursued by Bureau gunships. Osei sacrifices himself to buy them landing time, redeeming his betrayal. The beat is grief and awe at the silent, buried colony.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, climax. From Vesper's surface array, Freya must transmit the recovered massacre records system-wide, but the transmission requires routing through her own backup — which will overwrite her living memories with the archived ones. She chooses to burn her past so the future can't be edited. The beat is sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Navigator Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, resolution. Weeks later, the truth spreads; worlds reopen dialogue; the Bureau fractures. Freya navigates again, carrying gaps where her loved ones used to be, reading their names off a list like a stranger's. The beat is bittersweet survival: memory was the price, and it was worth paying.
